THE ONE THING TO ACT ON
Ethics approval S67821 on the keratinocyte project expires in 41 days. Two datasets and one draft inherit it and will be blocked from publication when it lapses.
WHAT THIS SCREEN CANNOT DO
You cannot read a researcher's private drafts, their reputation change log, or their contribution heat map from here. Governance means accountability for acts, not surveillance of people — the audit trail records what was done to artifacts, never what someone was working on.

1 · Data summary
Drafted from the project itself: 19 datasets, FCS and CSV, 14.2 GB, generated in-house. Edit if wrong.
2 · FAIR · findable and accessible
DOIs via DataCite, metadata public even under embargo, licence declared per dataset. Answered by how the platform works rather than by a promise.
3 · Interoperable and reusable
Tags bound to MeSH and Cellosaurus, CC-BY-4.0 default, method cards versioned with their own DOIs.
4 · Resources and costs · incomplete
Who pays for storage after the grant ends, and how much. Funders reject plans that leave this blank.
14.2 GB at institutional rates ≈ €38 / year
5 · Data security · incomplete
Mostly answerable from the institution's configuration. Two questions need a person: off-platform copies, and what happens to the physical samples.
6 · Ethical aspects
Pulled from the project's ethics record. Immortalised cell lines only, no human subjects.
THE PLAN STAYS TRUE BY ITSELF
Four of six sections are answered by what the platform can observe. Publish a dataset under a different licence and the DMP flags itself out of date — instead of sitting in a folder claiming something that stopped being true in 2025.

When this lapses, those three artifacts cannot be published or shared outside the lab until it is renewed. They are not deleted, not hidden, and remain fully usable inside the project — an expired approval is a publication constraint, not a data seizure.
INHERITANCE IS NOT A COPY
Change the expiry here and all four inheriting objects reflect it immediately. An artifact cannot be exported or handed over without carrying this reference with it.
WHO IS TOLD, AND WHEN
PI and research office at 90, 30 and 7 days. Once each. Nobody else — an expiring approval is not the whole lab's business.

18 PRE-REGISTRATION WITH TIME-STAMPED FREEZE (G19) 1440 × 620 · canvas region · before and after the freeze
LAB a frozen pre-registration is citable, and the freeze is the only thing that makes it worth anything Nucleofection at high passage/Pre-registration
BEFORE · EDITABLEDRAFT · 3 REVISIONS TODAY
HYPOTHESIS
Nucleofection maintains knock-in efficiency above 30% up to passage 28, where lipofection falls below 5% after passage 18.
PRIMARY OUTCOME · ONE ONLY
GFP⁺ / mCherry⁻ fraction at 48 h, gated per gate-and-quantify.R v3 with thresholds fixed in advance.
SAMPLE SIZE & POWER
n = 6 per passage, 4 passages. 80% power to detect a 15-point difference at α = 0.05.
ANALYSIS PLAN
Two-way ANOVA, passage × method. No subgroup analyses. Exclusion: viability below 85%.
While it is a draft, every revision is recorded but nothing is citable. The draft state is honest about being provisional — a pre-registration you can quietly edit is not a pre-registration.
AFTER · IMMUTABLEFROZEN & CITABLE
PREREG-0044 · v1
frozen 2026-09-09 11:02:14 UTC · sha 9c41…7ff
DOI10.5281/zenodo.8449 TIMESTAMPindependently anchored · verifiable without us FIRST DATAnot yet collected · that is the point DEVIATIONS0 · recorded openly if any occur
The frozen version is the one anyone cites. Later changes become v2 with a visible deviation note, never a silent edit — a reviewer can see what was decided before the data arrived and what changed after.
WHAT THE FREEZE LOCKS
Hypothesis, primary outcome, sample size, analysis plan, exclusion rules. Nothing about who does the work or when — those stay free to change.
WHY THIS MATTERS HERE
A pre-registered study that produces a null result is the strongest object this platform can hold: the expectation was on the record before the data existed.
